# Final Review Proposal
**Producer:** agent:codex/gpt-5.4

## Summary

Reviewed the dirty worktree under .claude/worktrees/tanksim-6e5.4.7. I found three issues: the submitted diff is implementing nitrification alkalinity work instead of the requested shrimp/molt bead, the new nitrogen-cycle trace uses the wrong nitrogen basis for alkalinity loss, and the new constant is now out of sync with the preset defaults. cargo test -p tank_core --test nitrification_alkalinity passes; the broader save_load_with_active_cycle_state failure reproduces on clean HEAD and appears unrelated.

## Amendments

1. Retarget the patch to the actual tanksim-6e5.6.3 deliverable. The current diff only adds nitrification/alkalinity bookkeeping and tests (crates/tank_core/src/systems/nitrogen_cycle.rs:12-23, crates/tank_core/src/engine.rs:229-239, crates/tank_core/src/types/process.rs:1-27, crates/tank_core/tests/nitrification_alkalinity.rs:1-336) and never reaches the shrimp/molt paths called out by the bead. As submitted, the acceptance criteria around mineral-driven molt success/failure, reserve/condition modifiers, failed-molt mortality, juvenile cadence, soft-vs-hard-water shrimp survival, and player-visible molt diagnostics remain unimplemented.
   Rationale: This is effectively the wrong feature set for the task prompt, so the requested deliverable is still missing.
2. Change the new nitrogen-cycle trace to emit the TAN-oxidation basis for alkalinity loss, not total_mg_n_nitrified. Engine now records nitrogen_cycle.total_n_nitrified_mg next to nitrogen_cycle.alk_consumed_meq (crates/tank_core/src/engine.rs:232-238), but total_mg_n_nitrified is computed as nob_step.oxidized_n_mg + comammox_step.oxidized_n_mg (crates/tank_core/src/systems/nitrogen_cycle.rs:343-346) while alkalinity is consumed from AOB + comammox TAN oxidation (crates/tank_core/src/systems/nitrogen_cycle.rs:15-23, crates/tank_core/src/systems/nitrogen_cycle.rs:366-384). In any tick where nitrite accumulates, the trace can show zero or low 'nitrified N' with nonzero alkalinity consumption, which makes the new diagnostics misleading.
   Rationale: The new observability is supposed to explain alkalinity depletion; right now the reported nitrogen value can contradict the reported alkalinity loss.
3. Keep the new alkalinity constant synchronized across the runtime and preset defaults. ProcessParams::default() now uses NITRIFICATION_ALK_MEQ_PER_MG_N (crates/tank_core/src/types/process.rs:337-338), but the shipped process preset still hardcodes 0.1428 in crates/tank_data/data/process/default.toml:52-54 and crates/tank_data/src/presets.rs:1015-1019, and scenario construction copies the preset value into ProcessParams (crates/tank_scenarios/src/lib.rs:346-392). That leaves two different 'default' initialization paths with slightly different chemistry behavior.
   Rationale: This creates a split source of truth immediately after introducing the named constant to be the authoritative stoichiometric parameter.
